{{Quote|The sky changes. War rages. Seasons pass. Voss die. Voss remains.|[[Rasan-Je]]|<ref name="Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref>}}
The '''Voss''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Voss|the same name]], in the [[Voss system/Legends|Voss system]] of the [[Allied Tion sector/Legends|Allied Tion sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Their [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] was [[Voss-Ka]], a fortified settlement atop a [[Mountain/Legends|mountain]]. Their totalitarian society was defended by [[Voss commandos|commandos]] and ruled by [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-wielding [[Voss Mystics|mystics]], who served as [[Force vision/Legends|seers]] and [[Force healing/Legends|healers]] and whom the other members of the species considered infallible. The Voss population was small, vastly outnumbered by their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld's]] other native group, the [[Gormak/Legends|Gormak]]&mdash;a species who saw the Voss as an aberration to be eliminated; however, both species eventually learned that the Voss were in fact offshoots of the Gormak. For [[Time/Legends|centuries]], the Voss fended off the assaults of the Gormak. Following the [[Treaty of Coruscant]] in [[3653 BBY]], which ended the [[Great Galactic War]] and started the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], off-worlders discovered the planet by chance, the Voss becoming known to both the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. The Empire attempted to [[Imperial Attack on Voss|conquer]] the planet, but their plans were thwarted by the secret interference of the [[Star Cabal]]; in the aftermath, both the Republic and the Empire believed the Voss were responsible for the invasion's defeat, and established diplomatic embassies on the planet.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|On Voss, our passions are suppressed until marriage. The Rite of Ardor awakens intensity and creates a bond between husband and wife.|[[Phi-Ton]]|<ref name="TOR" />}}
[[File:Yana-Ton.png|thumb|right|200px|A female Voss]]
Voss were [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]] with a high rate of [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitivity]] who displayed prominent sexual dimorphism. The male Voss had blue skin and bright orange eyes, while the females had red skin and azure blue eyes. The Voss did not have distinct pupils<ref name="TOR" /> and possessed unique patterns of markings on their face, neck, and body,<ref name="Creating">{{TORweb|url=news/blog/20100514_001|text=Creating Worlds|nolive=1}}</ref> a trace of their shared ancestry with [[Gormak/Legends|Gormak]].<ref name="Gormak and Voss Origins">{{TORcite|type=codex|Gormak and Voss Origins}}</ref> Their voices had a slight mechanical tinge to it, making them sound somewhat like a [[Droid/Legends|droid]] or machine. Voss underwent a physical, developmental change during their [[Marriage/Legends|marriage]] ceremonies and did not develop [[Gender/Legends|sexually]] prior to the performance of these rituals.<ref name="Creating" /> With training, the Voss were able to access the [[Spirit World]] that existed on their homeworld to appear in faraway locations or to manifest as spirits after their death.<ref name="TOR" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|No Voss is perfect. No Voss is above vision.|[[Medo-Ja]]|<ref name="TOR" />}}
[[File:Amin-Le.png|thumb|left|200px|A Voss Mystic]]
The Voss [[Species/Legends|species]] resided in an isolated [[Mountain/Legends|mountain]]-top [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Voss-Ka]] and was vastly outnumbered on their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] by its other native sentient species, the [[Gormak/Legends|Gormak]], who were extremely hostile toward them.<ref name="TOR" /> Most Voss live peacefully in Voss-Ka, caring for their families, cultivating the wild plants and maintaining equipment for the [[Voss commandos]] in the war against the Gormak,<ref name="Voss-Ka">{{TORcite|type=codex|Voss-Ka}}</ref> although some Voss did live outside the capital city, such as the [[Voss Mystics]] who resided in the [[Shrine of Healing]]. The Voss were great lovers of art, and their architecture featured a distinctive artistic style that had existed for thousands of years before contact with the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] and [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]],<ref name="TOR" /> featuring monochromatic patterns with heavy reliance on symbolism.<ref name="Creating" /> All Voss had two short names, connected by a hyphen, with the family name being the second one. For example, [[Bas-Ton]] was the brother of [[Therod-Ton]] and father of [[Phi-Ton]] and [[Yana-Ton]], all of whom were descended from [[Zhi-Ton]].<ref name="TOR" /> Voss marriage ceremony known as the [[Rite of Ardor]] had the effect of fully awakening any mating instinct within the Voss that was typically suppressed in their society. As such, the Voss did not feel traits such as physical attraction until the ritual was conducted.<ref name="The Sacred Flame">{{TORcite|type=class|Imperial Agent|The Sacred Flame|Voss}}</ref> Voss tended to be reserved, speaking very little, except during [[Funeral/Legends|funeral]] rites and times of hardship, when Voss became outwardly emotional.<ref name="Creating" />

===Voss Mystics===
{{Quote|The Mystics are never wrong.|[[Shanatka-Lo]]|<ref name="TOR" />}}
[[File:Vana-Xo_healing.png|thumb|right|200px|A Voss Mystic performs the healing ritual.]]
The entire Voss society was guided by [[Force vision/Legends|Force visions]] of [[Voss Mystics]], which were considered infallible without exception. The role of the Mystics dominated the life of Voss, with many potentials undergoing years of training and trials to become Mystics, ending in a pilgrimage across Voss, in which the potentials visited holy sites in the dangerous [[Gormak Lands]] and learned from their elders. The trials were dangerous, and some acolytes died while others failed, but those who passed the trials returned triumphantly to Voss-Ka to be recognized by the [[Three]] and joined the ranks of Mystics. Mystics often lived in seclusion of the [[Tower of Prophecy]] in Voss-Ka or at the [[Shrine of Healing]] in the [[Old Paths]], the only significant Voss presence on the planet outside their capital. When Mystics experienced the rare visions, they were passed to the experienced [[Interpreter (Voss)|Interpreters]] at the Tower of Prophecy to discern their meaning, who debated and meditated for as long as took before presenting their analysis to the Three, who acted on a decision which all Voss followed without exception.<ref name="Mystics">{{TORcite|type=codex|Mystics}}</ref> While visions were believed to always serve the greater good of the Voss people, in the short term they could bring great suffering. Over recoded Voss history, some visons led to a bloody civil war, mass starvations and destruction of half of Voss-Ka, but even that was only to spare the Voss from a worse fate, as a vision was never proven wrong, and ignoring them led to an even greater peril.<ref name="Mystic Visions">{{TORcite|type=codex|Mystic Visions}}</ref>

In the [[Shrine of Healing]] the Mystics developed and practiced [[Voss healing ritual]] that allowed them to mend even the gravest of wounds, but at the cost of transferring the strength of another to heal the patient.<ref name="Mystics" /> Based on the [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]] technology, the Mystics created the [[Vitalicron/Legends|vitalicrons]], machines designed to carry the memory and visions of those who went through the healing practices of the Mystics, which were then stored in the vault at the Shrine of Healing.<ref name="TOR" /> Entire floors of the Shrine had special rooms with purpose known only to the Mystics, some of them dedicated for trials of potential Mystics or the [[Trial of the First Commando]].<ref name="Shrine of Healing">{{TORcite|type=codex|Shrine of Healing}}</ref> An outcast sect of the Mystics called the [[Dream-walkers]], not entirely embraced by the [[Voss]] society, practiced the ritual of [[Dream-walking]] in their encampment in the [[Mind healer's grove]] beneath [[Voss-Ka]]. Another ritual of the Mystics could restore even the most fractured mind, but was [[Forbidden Ritual|forbidden]] because it involved dream-walking alongside a [[Gormak/Legends|Gormak]], and was guarded by the Mystic [[Mar-Da]].<ref>{{TORcite|type=class|Sith Inquisitor|The Ritual|Voss}}</ref> Despite their reliance upon and veneration of Force prophecies, the Voss held no formal knowledge of the Force and were uninterested in learning from either the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] or the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]].<ref name="Voss">{{Holonet|planets|voss|Voss}}</ref> The Voss Mystics were considered to be [[Gray Jedi|gray]] by the Jedi and the Sith for their non-standard perspective on the nature of the Force, as they belonged to neither order nor fully embraced either the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]] or [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark]] sides of the Force.<ref name="Creating" />

===Voss commandos===
{{Quote|I serve the will of the Mystics. As did my husband. Our names will be joined forever in song.|[[Tala-Reh]]|<ref name="TOR" />}}
[[File:Rade_Sa.png|thumb|left|200px|A Voss Commando]]
The Voss society revolved around their constant struggle to survive against the Gormak onslaught and although the Gormak sought the utter destruction of the Voss, Voss society held a strict law against attempting to wipe the Gormak out due to one of the visions of the mystics.<ref name="Gormak">{{HolonetOld|inhabitants|gormak|Gormak}}</ref> Other than the Mystics, all adult Voss served a mandatory term as the [[Voss commandos]], who defended Voss-Ka and its people against endless Gormak hordes. After their term some Voss returned to civilian lives, while other chose to stay and become commanding officers. All commandos were trained as [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] and in [[Unarmed combat|hand-to-hand combat]], ensuring that every Voss was capable of defending themselves and understood the sacrifice necessary for the survival of their people.<ref name="Voss Commandos">{{TORcite|type=codex|Voss Commandos}}</ref> Voss commandos maintained multiple fortified outposts across the wildernes of Voss,<ref name="TOR" /> while a special cadre of commandos protected the Shrine of Healing, patrolling the nearby hills for Gormak ambushes.<ref name="Shrine of Healing" /> The Voss were governed by the [[Three]], who were chosen for either years, weeks or even hours according to the visions of the Mystics, and acted on the reports of the Interpreters, having little day-to-day contact with the Mystics themselves. Working from the Tower of Prophecy, the Three administered Voss-Ka, made policy decisions and coordinated the endless war against the Gormak.<ref name="The Three">{{TORcite|type=codex|The Three}}</ref> Voss laws were established by the Mystics, enforced by the commandos and judged by the [[adjudicators]], a group created specifically for offworlders, as no Voss citizen would ever violate their rulers' edicts.<ref name="Law">{{TORcite|type=codex|Law and Order on Voss (Smuggler)}}</ref> The Voss viewed local predators [[mawvorr]] as their guardians or protectors due to their tendencies to attack the Gormak on sight and took steps to maintain the mawvorr population around Voss-Ka.<ref name="Mawvorr">{{TORcite|type=codex|Mawvorr}}</ref> Between the strong defenses and artistry of their home, as well as the guidance of their mystics, members of Voss society were generally pleased with the rule of the Voss Mystics, despite the totalitarian nature of their government.<ref name="Creating" />

==History==
===Eternal War===
{{Quote|The last Gormak must not die. There was no discussion. The interpretation was clear. If every Gormak dies, every Voss dies. This is true. Wage war but do not win. Survive. For total victory is death.|[[Jadek-To]]|<ref name="TOR" />}}
[[File:Nemok-Ta.png|thumb|right|200px|The Voss were descendant from ancient Gormak taught to use the Force.]]
In ancient times, at some point after the [[Second Great Schism]], the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] came to Voss, which at that point had only one native sentient [[Species/Legends|species]], the [[Gormak/Legends|Gormak]], whom the Sith viewed as primitive and ignored as they began to harvest the world's resources. However, the planet and the Gormak were irrevocably changed when the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] arrived and attempted to drive the Sith off Voss. Seeking allies among the natives, the Jedi agreed to teach some of the Gormak tribes how to use [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], but the Gormak were unprepared for the knowledge. Those tribes underwent radical evolutionary changes within a few generations, becoming a new species named the Voss. The Jedi attempted to teach the Voss how to control their emotions and new powers, but the Voss instead attacked the Sith on the planet, bringing the new species in contact with the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. This caused the dark side to become manifest in a Sith structure on the planet, and this entity came to take the name [[Sel-Makor]] as it gained intelligence.<ref name="Gormak and Voss Origins" /> Sel-Makor began to feed on violence and suffering, fueling its dark side powers and spreading corruption across the surrounding area, which became known as the [[Nightmare Lands]], and the ancient Sith complex that the entity inhabited was known as the [[Dark Heart]].<ref name="The Dark Heart">{{TORcite|type=codex|The Dark Heart}}</ref> After the extermination of the Sith, the Voss forgot their origins and founded the city of Voss-Ka atop the planet's highest peak, while the Jedi eventually died out or departed.<ref name="Gormak and Voss Origins" /> Sel-Makor, meanwhile, influenced the Gormak's bloodlust and drove the far more numerous species to attack their cousins throughout the centuries so that he could feed off of their dark emotions.<ref name="Visions of Light and Darkness">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Visions of Light and Darkness|Voss}}</ref>

===Cold War===
{{Quote|Outsiders rarely impress.|[[Rade-Sa]]|<ref name="TOR" />}}
[[File:Laeras-Wu.png|thumb|left|200px|Long-dead Voss could manifest themselves to the living through the Spirit World.]]
Following the [[Treaty of Coruscant]] that ended the [[Great Galactic War]] between the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], Voss was accidentally rediscovered by the larger [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]<ref name="Imperial Attack" /> around [[3645 BBY]].<ref name="Voss-Date">{{TORcite|type=class|Imperial Agent|Paying Respects|Voss}} establishes that the [[Bas-Ton (imposter)|imposter Bas-Ton]] has been on [[Voss]] for five years, and he was sent there to infiltrate [[Voss (species)|Voss]] society after the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire's]] invasion of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] failed. Additionally, ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]'' places the events of Act III, which include Voss, in approximately [[3640 BBY]]; thus, the invasion of Voss occurred in approximately [[3645 BBY]].</ref> Upon learning of the Voss' prophetic abilities, Sith Emperor [[Tenebrae|Vitiate]] ordered to [[Imperial Attack on Voss|conquer]] the planet,<ref name="Request an Audience">{{TORcite|type=class|Sith Warrior|Request An Audience|Voss}}</ref> and [[General/Legends|General]] [[Khypes]] arrived in orbit with a [[Battlecruiser/Legends|battlecruiser]] and several [[Army/Legends|army]] divisions in order to demand a surrender, having been alerted that the Voss capital of Voss-Ka was undefended. However, Khypes' cruiser exploded before he could contact the planet, and the ship's escorts were destroyed moments later. Realizing that they had underestimated the Voss, the Empire declared that Khypes had gone rogue, and both the Empire and the Republic began making diplomatic overtures to the Voss.<ref name="Imperial Attack">{{TORcite|type=codex|The Imperial Attack on Voss}}</ref> The Voss decided not to allow these "Outsiders" into the Voss-Ka proper, but rather set a special [[Alien Enclave]] for them, containing both [[Republic Embassy (Voss)|Republic]] and [[Imperial Embassy (Voss)|Imperial Embassy]].<ref name="Voss-Ka" /> The Voss species successfully maintained the neutrality of their planet, but the presence of the outsiders required the Voss to create [[Adjudicators]] specifically to govern the actions of the outsiders, with dangerous offenders force to take the [[Step of Harmony]] off the mountain into the gorge below. Since the Voss treated all outsiders equally, crime syndicates such as the [[Exchange]] could operate freely on the planet where Republic and Imperial law was not enforced, as long as they were not caught breaking the laws of the Voss.<ref name="Law" />

However, their efforts to gain Voss Mystics on their side were foiled by a secret society calling iteself the [[Star Cabal]]. An operative named [[Albathius]] arrived on Voss shortly after its discovery, and gained great influence among the Mystics, becoming known as the "Shining Man" and convincing the Voss to stay neutral from the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between two governments for three thousand days, enough time for the Star Cabal to exert its own influence on the war and keeping the Voss from choosing a side. The Shining Man promised that in time, the Gormak, the Empire and the Republic would be eradicated, and no offworlders would come to Voss again, and was buried under [[Voss-Ka]] after his death.<ref name="The Prophecy of the Shining Man">{{TORcite|type=class|Imperial Agent|The Prophecy of the Shining Man|Voss}}</ref> Not outsiders all came to Voss seeking a formal alliance or attempting to exploit their lax laws, as many offworlders also flocked to Voss in hopes of being cured of various ailments and afflictions untreatable elsewhere in the galaxy. They were forced to embark on a dangerous pilgrimage to the Shrine of Healing, necessary for the [[Voss healing ritual]] to take proper effect. The trials purified the spirit of the petitioner, ensuring that their affliction was dispersed amongst the ritual participants, rather than passed onto them.<ref name="Pilgrimage">{{TORcite|type=codex|The Pilgrimage to the Shrine of Healing}}</ref>

===Galactic War===
{{Quote|The Mystics have a vision. An outsider will end the threat of the Gormak.|[[Laryn-Ki]]|<ref name="TOR" />}}
[[File:The_Three.png|thumb|right|250px|The Three during the Galactic War]]
Both galactic powers continued their diplomatic efforts on Voss until the Cold War ended and two governments engaged in another [[Galactic War]] elsewhere in the galaxy, while struggling to maintain neutrality on Voss. By [[3640 BBY]]<ref name="date">{{TOR dates|Voss}}</ref> the Three consisted of [[Sonn-Vi]], [[Gunta-Mer]], and [[Nen-Ji]].<ref name="The Three" /> During that year [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Fulminiss]] learned the Voss healing ritual from the spirits of long-dead Mystics, and corrupted the ritual so that it twisted minds and drove its victims insane.<ref name="Bloody Pilgrimage">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Bloody Pilgrimage|Voss}}</ref> Fulminiss traveled to the Dark Heart in order to meet with Sel-Makor, where he [[Mission to the Dark Heart (Hero of Tython)|fell]] to the [[Lightsaber/Legends|blade]] of the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] known as the [[Hero of Tython]], while Voss Commando [[Tala-Reh]] sacrificed herself to destroy Sel-Makor for good.<ref name="Visions of Light and Darkness" /> Sith Lord [[Torius]] attempted to hold Voss-Ka hostage with a [[ZR-57 orbital strike bomb]] planted underneath the city, but the Mystic [[Ki-Ve]] foresaw that this plan would fail and the Voss did not intervene, allowing Torius to be stopped by [[Republic Special Forces Division]] [[Havoc Squad]].<ref name="Into the Shadows">{{TORcite|type=class|Trooper|Into the Shadows|Voss}}</ref> Trying to gain an alliance with the Voss, both the Republic and the Empire lent aid to the Voss in their fight against the Gormak, the Sith aiding the Voss in destroying ''[[Gormegan-1]]'', a [[Starship/Legends|starship]] built by the Gormak on Gormak King [[Jokull]]'s orders,<ref name="Space Race">{{TORcite|type=faction|Imperial|Space Race|Voss}}</ref> while the Republic helped the Voss to destroy the [[Gormak cannon|cannon]] the Gormak were building to use against Voss-Ka.<ref name="In the Crosshairs">{{TORcite|type=faction|Republic|In the Crosshairs|Voss}}</ref> However, in the process, the Voss discovered Jokull's ability to see the future, and enlisted the aid of outsiders in retracing the Gormak king's steps in the Nightmare Lands, soon learning the truth of their species' creation.<ref name="The Dark Hollow">{{TORcite|type=faction|Republic|The Dark Hollow|Voss}}</ref><ref name="A Long Forgotten Evil">{{TORcite|type=faction|Imperial|A Long Forgotten Evil|Voss}}</ref>

===The Eternal Empire===
{{Quote|The Mystics will stay. The Commandos will join the Alliance in battle.|[[Sana-Rae]]|<ref name="Eternal Throne">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Eternal Throne]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Vara-Sol.png|thumb|left|200px|A Voss who succumbed to the corrupting influence of the Nightmare Lands]]
In [[3636 BBY]]<ref name="KOTFE date">{{TOR updates|4.0}}</ref> the galaxy was [[Eternal Empire conquest|invaded]] by the [[Eternal Empire]] of [[Zakuul]] that subjugated both the Republic and the Sith Empire within a year and placed dozens of massive [[Battle station/Legends|battle stations]] called [[Star Fortress]]es in orbits of subjugated worlds to watch for possible uprisings.<ref name="KOTFE 4">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|chapter=4}}</ref> [[Voss Star Fortress]] was commanded by [[Exarch]] [[Andur Melor]] and protected by a [[Voss shield bunker|shield bunker]] located in the [[Pelath-Ri Marches]].<ref name="Resistance">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=general|Voss: The Resistance|Voss}}</ref> In the face of a larger threat, the Voss and Gormak soldiers had united to defend their homeworld, ending the centuries-long war between the two species. Their alliance has proven surprisingly effective, with the meditative reserve of the Voss complimenting the ferocious strength of the Gormak to form a formidable army.<ref>{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=codex|Voss-Gormak Alliance}}</ref> In [[3630 BBY]],<ref>{{TOR updates|5.0}}</ref> Eternal Empress Vaylin launched an [[Invasion of Voss]], determined to hunt her brother [[Arcann]] and mother [[Senya Tirall]] who had taken refuge at the Shrine of Healing. Operatives of the [[Eternal Alliance|Alliance]] that opposed Zakuul were already onworld, allowing the Alliance to scramble their fleet in response. The [[Eternal Fleet]] bombarded Voss-Ka and deployed ground troops in the city, and [[Theron Shan]] attempted to rally Voss commandos to its defense, but their forces were outmatched, and were forced to take shelter in the Tower of Prophecy along with the Mystic [[Sana-Rae]]. At the Shrine of Healing, Voss Mystics transferred Senya Tirall's strength to Arcann, healing his injuries and mending his broken spirit, allowing him to flee to his shuttle and escape into [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. Vaylin has ordered the Eternal Fleet to burn her entire family regardless of casualties on Voss, but the tide of the battle was turned by the arrival of the [[Imperial Navy (Sith Empire)|Imperial Fleet]] that opened fire on the [[Eternal Fleet warship]]s, destroying several of them and prompting the rest to flee in self-preservation. Although Voss was saved from the full destructive might of the Eternal Throne, it suffered heavy losses, with much of the planet devastated and thousands of Voss and Gormak killed.<ref name="KOTET 1">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|chapter=1}}</ref>

==Voss in the galaxy==
{{Quote|When my vision showed I must take many Voss, seek an Outsider, and enter a war, great caution was exercised. My vision was given to five different interpreters. All five interpretations aligned. Thus, I am here.|[[Sana-Rae]]|<ref name="Fallen Empire">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Fallen Empire]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Gaden-Ko.png|thumb|right|200px|Mystic Gaden-Ko assisted the Rift Alliance in the Battle of Corellia]]
After being exposed to the larger galaxy, several Voss left their homeworld to travel and explore the galaxy. [[Cavrus-Til]] traveled to the Republic capital of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], while [[Azula-Hej]] visited [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].<ref name="Paying Your Debts">{{TORcite|type=class|Smuggler|Paying Your Debts|Voss}}</ref> In [[3640 BBY]]<ref name="KOTFE date" /> mystic-in-training Gaden-Ko was just starting his pilgrimage, when he lost all of his bodyguards at the [[Holy Path of Mir]], after which the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi]] Consular known as [[the Barsen'thor]] offered to protect him on his pilgrimage<ref name="A Thorny Path">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Consular|A Thorny Path|Voss}}</ref> and guided Gaden-Ko to become a Mystic. His first vision showed Gaden-Ko that his destiny was to help his new friend and the Galactic Republic in the [[Galactic War]] with the Sith Empire. Gaden-Ko gained a small entourage of Voss Commandos, healers, and interpreters as he joined the Barsen'thor's [[Rift Alliance]],<ref name="Deep Cradle, Dark Heart">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Consular|Deep Cradle, Dark Heart|Voss}}</ref> participating in the [[Capture of the Javelin]] and the [[Battle of Corellia]] during the [[Hunt for the Children]] of the Emperor.<ref name="Shattering">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Consular|Shattering|The ''Javelin''}}</ref>

Later same year [[Darth Malgus]] proclaimed a new [[New Empire]], and the top Sith [[Ambassador/Legends|ambassador]] on Voss [[Darth Serevin]] joined his cause and convinced some of the Mystics to follow him. [[Talsa-ko|Talsa-Ko]] and [[Queneth Li]] traveled with Darth Serevin to [[Ilum/Legends|Ilum]] in the middle of the [[Battle of Ilum]], where Talsa-Ko had a vision of bowing to the victor of a battle between Darth Serevin and his attackers. Eager to fulfill the vision, Serevin engaged the intruders at [[Fort Barrow]], but was killed alongside Queneth-Li, leaving Talsa-Ko to beg the attackers to spare her life.<ref name="TOR" /> In [[3631 BBY]]<ref name="KOTFE date" /> Mystic [[Sana-Rae]] experienced a vision that showed her help Voss by joining the [[Eternal Alliance|Alliance]] that opposed the [[Eternal Empire]] of [[Zakuul]]. She traveled to the [[Alliance base]] on [[Odessen]] and was put in charge of the Alliance's Force enclave, overseeing the training of her fellow Mystics, as well as other Force-sensitives.<ref name="KOTFE 9">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|chapter=9}}</ref> Being a Voss, and thus not aligned to either [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]] or the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], Sana-Rae was well respected by her peers, able to build up a cooperation of Sith and Jedi alike, and eventually fulfilled her vision by helping the Alliance save Voss from destruction by the Eternal Fleet.<ref name="KOTET 1" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Voss are a new species created for ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' [[Star Wars video games|video game]] by [[BioWare]], and were first introduced in [[the Holonet]] article on the game's website.<ref name="Voss" /> The Voss are the result of BioWare writers' desire to add something new to ''[[Star Wars]]'' lore in the game, although they selected an obscure planet rather than creating one from scratch. The appearance of the Voss species was inspired from that of [[Wikipedia:Poison dart frog|poison dart frogs]]. The overall presentation of the Voss was designed to make them feel isolated and harried by outside forces, and to have a mystic culture. Originally, mystics were considered as a player-controllable class but were rejected in favor of the [[Imperial Agent]] because there were already four other Force-using classes planned for the game.<ref name="Creating" />
